skill.name: polars
skill.description: Guides Polars DataFrame work with expressions, lazy queries, joins, I/O, aggregations, and pandas migration patterns.
skill.summary: Build faster Polars data pipelines with practical DataFrame patterns and migration guidance.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Reviewed all 95 static findings and found documentation false positives rather than executable malicious behavior. The matches come from Markdown code fences, placeholder cloud credential examples, Polars list.eval usage, and performance guidance. No prompt injection or semantic evidence of data exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: Cloud storage examples assign placeholder secrets through environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Show credential setup as external configuration and warn users not to hardcode real secrets.

remediation.issue: The Polars list.eval example can be mistaken for dynamic code execution by scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Add a note that list.eval evaluates Polars expressions and does not run Python eval.

static_findings.snippet: For additional best practices and patterns, load `references/best_practices.md`.
- `core_concepts.md` - Detailed explanations of expressions, lazy evaluation, and type system
- `operations.md` - Comprehensive guide to all common operations with examples
- `pandas_migration.md` - Complete migration guide from pandas to Polars
- `io_guide.md` - Data I/O operations for all supported formats
- `transformations.md` - Joins, concatenation, pivots, and reshaping operations

content.value_statement: Data teams need fast guidance when building Polars pipelines and migrating from pandas. This skill provides concise patterns for expressions, lazy queries, I/O, joins, and performance tuning.
actual_capabilities: Explains Polars expressions, eager DataFrames, and lazy LazyFrames.
Provides patterns for select, filter, with_columns, group_by, joins, and window operations.
Covers CSV, Parquet, JSON, database, and cloud storage I/O examples.
Maps common pandas workflows to equivalent Polars patterns.
Highlights performance practices such as predicate pushdown, projection pushdown, and streaming.
Documents reshaping, nested data, null handling, and type usage patterns.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a live Polars execution environment.
It does not validate queries against a real dataset or schema.
Cloud and database examples use placeholders and require user configuration.
Version-specific Polars behavior may need confirmation against installed package docs.

use_cases.title: Migrate pandas pipelines
use_cases.description: Convert common pandas selection, filtering, grouping, and transformation patterns into idiomatic Polars workflows.

use_cases.title: Optimize large data processing
use_cases.description: Use lazy scans, column pruning, predicate pushdown, and streaming to improve large dataset workflows.

use_cases.title: Build data ingestion recipes
use_cases.description: Choose practical patterns for reading and writing CSV, Parquet, JSON, databases, and cloud storage.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Polars task
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me solve this data task with Polars. Explain the recommended DataFrame steps and note when lazy evaluation would help.

prompt_templates.title: Convert pandas to Polars
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert my pandas workflow to Polars. Explain the key API differences and preserve the original data transformation intent.

prompt_templates.title: Improve pipeline performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Polars pipeline for performance. Focus on lazy scans, early filtering, column selection, streaming, and native expressions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a production query plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a robust Polars workflow for a large multi-file dataset. Include I/O format choices, joins, aggregations, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: I need to process a large CSV and keep only recent rows and five columns.
output: Use a lazy scan so Polars can optimize the query before reading data.
Filter rows and select needed columns early to reduce memory pressure.
Write the result to Parquet when downstream tools can read it.

output_examples.input: I want to migrate a pandas groupby aggregation to Polars.
output: Use group_by with expression aggregations instead of pandas apply patterns.
Name aggregate outputs clearly with aliases.
Avoid Python callbacks unless no native expression exists.

output_examples.input: I need to join two datasets and reshape the result.
output: Choose the join type based on row preservation requirements.
Check join keys for type compatibility before combining data.
Use pivot or unpivot patterns after the join when the analysis needs a new shape.

best_practices: Prefer lazy scans for large files so Polars can optimize reads and transformations.
Use native expressions instead of Python callbacks for speed and parallel execution.
Select required columns early and choose efficient file formats such as Parquet.
anti_patterns: Do not translate pandas code line by line without checking Polars expression semantics.
Do not use Python row functions for operations that native expressions can handle.
Do not hardcode real cloud credentials or database secrets in examples or generated code.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps create and review Polars DataFrame workflows for analysis, migration, I/O, and performance tuning.

faq.question: Can it execute Polars code?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Execution depends on the connected coding environment.

faq.question: Does it support pandas migration?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains common pandas to Polars mappings and highlights semantic differences.

faq.question: Does it cover lazy evaluation?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains LazyFrame usage, query optimization, predicate pushdown, projection pushdown, and streaming.

faq.question: Does it include cloud storage examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents S3, Azure, and Google Cloud Storage patterns using placeholder configuration values.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
